newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BONDS END QUIET DAY LOWER, SEEN DRIFTING.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BONDS END QUIET DAY LOWER, SEEN DRIFTING.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds ended a fairly quiet day lower, in line with most of its European neighbours, but the Bund spread narrowed and traders said they saw the market edging gently downwards.
"The market feels soft," one trader said. "I think it will drift lower. There was no real money involved today."

Traders were at a loss to explain the sudden rash of negative sentiment in the market, although some noted a negative market commentary on Tuesday from JP Morgan which said OLOs would underperform German Bunds.
"It is like a self-fulfilling prophecy," one said.
Traders said there had been some activity in the shorter maturities, but only sporadic interest elsewhere.
They said earlier there had been a big seller in five-year paper.
Traders said they expected to market to remain dejected at least ahead of U.S. February producer prices which are due on Friday.

The yield of the benchmark 2007 OLO was 5.77 percent against Tuesday's 5.74, and the spread over Bunds widened to 10 basis points from eight. The March futures contract was 28 basis points down at 122.00. -- Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810
